summary: 1. Two new meeting notes landed — a weekly production planning meeting and a shift meeting, both 31-Aug. 2. Shovels missed the 60/20 productivity target on all six days reviewed this week; truck fleet utilization and shovel productivity were named the primary drivers of a below-plan week, with drilling also behind (4,000m needed on the day vs. a 19,000m weekly target the team called unlikely). 2. 3. The shovel-productivity shortfall produced a live disagreement rather than a shared diagnosis: one view puts Stage 4 excavators at ~80% buckets-down waiting on trucks in the confined Block 171/172 access; a counter-observation from a site walk found only one truck on the platform. 4. Both sides agreed to share queuing-time data before the next review. 5. A separate block-numbering discrepancy surfaced in the same meeting — Geology calls the block 173, blasting calls it 174, confirmed to actually be 172. 3. 6. Same day, same working area: a truck transmission failure at Block 172 (3.5-hour delay) and four tires lost to cuts/punctures, with fragmentation quality at Block 172 named as a contributing factor for the first time in this KB's tire-damage thread (previously always road condition or spillage). 4. 7. On shift: dumper 1-to-9 is stuck in a blast radius (recovery reassigned to the new superintendent since the usual contact is on training) and dumper 429 is stuck in the loading area; Dispatch was criticised directly for not communicating machine status, with updates instead coming from Peter. 8. A 720-litre diesel delay was attributed to maintenance. 9. A new overspill-bench loading proposal near a high wall (cones, 3-5m buffer, prior rock-bounce-onto-road incident cited) mirrors this KB's existing standard overspill control set almost exactly. 5. Workforce-tracking discipline was reinforced at both meetings — daily absentee tracking by name, the no-work-no-pay principle, and the clinic documentation policy (no written hospital note has ever actually been produced on site). A PM confrontation over machine bucket efficiency produced a usable coaching example (stay calm, ask what can be improved) and flagged an English-language barrier for one named foreman. Three already ingested at prior passes (Mine Site Safety & Operations Meeting Summary, Mining Operations Review: August Performance & Recovery Plan, Mining Operations Site Meeting — all 30-Aug). Two genuinely new, both created 31-Aug: "Mining Operations Weekly Production Planning Meeting" and "Open-Pit Mining Operations Shift Meeting" — both written verbatim to RAW.
